That's why we must unite to support strong Senate candidates in the midterm elections. Not the candidates hand-picked by the Washington machine. We need fighters — proven by their records, battle-tested, and ready to take on the establishment. The Senate Conservatives Fund has endorsed a strong group of them, and we need your help to get them across the finish line. Here's who's in the fight:

# Nate Morris

# U.S. Senate | Kentucky

---
# May 19 (Primary)

---
Mitch McConnell's seat is finally open, and Nate Morris is making sure another establishment Republican doesn't fill it. He built a $700 million company from a $10,000 line of credit, and he's running on mass deportation, a full immigration moratorium, and zero tolerance for career politicians. The primary is on May 19. This race is winnable — and your support can deliver the knockout blow to McConnell's failed legacy.
---
|

# Barry Moore
---
# U.S. Senate | Alabama

---
# May 19 (Primary)

---
Congressman Barry Moore was the first elected official in America to endorse Donald Trump — at the 2015 Mobile rally, before anyone believed Trump could win. He carries a 98% Heritage Action score, Trump's full endorsement, and a lifetime of fighting for conservative values. He currently leads the primary field by 6 points, but with 47% of voters still undecided, money matters.

|

---
# Kevin Hern
---
# U.S. Senate | Oklahoma

# June 16 (Primary)
---
A McDonald's franchisee who built a business empire, Congressman Kevin Hern chaired the Republican Study Committee and carries a 95% Heritage Action score. Trump endorsed him two days after he launched — along with SCF heroes like Senators Ron Johnson (R-WI) and Rick Scott (R-FL). If Hern wins, he will be one of the strongest America First voices in the Senate.

# Harriet Hageman
---
# U.S. Senate | Wyoming

# August 18 (Primary)
---
Congresswoman Harriet Hageman crushed RINO Liz Cheney 66-29%. Now she's bringing that same fight to the Senate. A fourth-generation Wyoming rancher with 34 years of battling federal overreach, Hageman has a 98% Heritage Action score and Trump's endorsement from day one. This is a once-in-a-generation chance to send a proven MAGA warrior to the upper chamber.
---
|
---
---
# Ashley Moody
---
# U.S. Senate | Florida

---
# August 18 (Primary)
---
As Florida's Attorney General, Ashley Moody was the first in the nation to demand fentanyl be declared a weapon of mass destruction — and the first to demand Biden designate the cartels as foreign terrorists (Trump did it on Day 1). Now she's in the Senate, fighting to stay. Her 2026 special election is one conservatives cannot afford to lose.
---
|
---
---
# Roger Marshall
---
# U.S. Senate | Kansas

---
# August 4 (Primary)
---
Senator Roger "Doc" Marshall is leading the biggest election integrity fight in the Senate right now. He's championing the SAVE America Act — requiring proof of citizenship to vote — and he's willing to launch a talking filibuster to force a vote. When every single Senate Democrat voted against a clean voter ID bill, Marshall called them out. He's also fighting to stop China from buying American farmland.
---
|
---
---
# Bill Hagerty
---
# U.S. Senate | Tennessee

---
# August 6 (Primary)
---
Senator Bill Hagerty just hosted President Trump in Memphis to celebrate a landmark win: the Memphis Safe Task Force drove overall crime down 43%, robberies down 51%, and car thefts down 67% — and located 150 missing children. He's also authored the BIOSECURE Act to exclude Chinese military-linked biotech firms from federal contracts. Hagerty is delivering, and he needs our support.

subject: I’m the only U.S Senate candidate that speaks this way
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ROYCE WHITE FOR SENATE
body:
It’s the corrupt world against us |
---

Peter,

I'm the only U.S. Senate candidate in America that speaks this way. I don't take money from AIPAC or the Muslim Brotherhood. I'm probably on a CCP watchlist and the DC uniparty says I'm "unqualified", which is the best endorsement I could hope for in America. We have to rally this country, right here, right now.

[](https://links.iterable.com/u/click?_t=ce1ce9e616484205a28a45cfaf96cecf&_m=0e696f637f954be98847e3a2286befc7&_e=W1luWzOEBEhb64rVso1It7RIDkdQAoapd3P_t_egX1M0Yk201A8bDG_mQGChBcYLN0XAq8FjmyIWZh8RHpoO3csOu6XK3DsbaPgnkT8aoU35865syXvANcDutJ9js7vPlnGXq2RSt09XpGs34D3LcsYIZnfm5haBed37AxKo-n8ATJhCdGi2_nJ9fKTacrBNSOxWTAbRpUF4bN3YMij712I8PfcbcQm739T4ROBzEIkF4zVG8_TjIPPRTyqjsCcjF2GaDrzHx_x5Y1gI_H_M0f3GN85AN8Oc5CSP4m_981CUs_-iloxwCb6Bruy_PHGkwOGuWFwpLLUlFeBYs2CECfQjX8VwYJN06XFNSgE5O3jSd2ebXIbowQ-rUxuZglat4A3nlpmcQGP4qmJdbNkJL1zk9tMSrFbdvycQb3GeOdxC3x0ST9AnwEbQcdVcRAIJfF54Jy8sFFXKpiO3fhwVAmHM2YyNimKTotzNblcrzc6VuSuSX5FyC3d9yiWmEv-giyWnZpAlwVKroOrr36S41qQWcSuK-tCziV4_zdW0jCk%3D)
We may have to start a new party with this idea in the foundations, but I'd much rather save The Republican Party. Why? I genuinely believe in the philosophy of Republicanism. The fundamental issue in America is certainly a 2 party system that is perverted and corrupted beyond recognition. Maybe beyond salvaging, but... A core component of that decay is the size of government itself and more importantly the administrative leviathan that powers it. A basic yet almost unquantifiable difference between the Republican Party and Democratic Party is Democrats have conceded to the infinite expansion of the federal government as a principle. The Republicans, at least in theory and for show, still pretend we believe in shrinking the government. Right now, I don't know how many Republicans really believe in that. We must starve and strangle this leviathan and the corruption that undergirds it.

I'm trying to help this party and our country through the mechanisms we have... if we fail to rally behind good ideas things are going to get bad. Right now the Republican Party seems much more interested in Forever Wars and Legacy Media than America. Which is obviously a losing position politically and maybe militarily. Maybe that's the whole point, throw the ball back and forth with We The People as the monkey in the middle. Gavin Newsom? Really? Is anybody else sick of this crap? **[Drop a $10 donation if you see the intention.](https://links.iterable.com/u/click?_t=ce1ce9e616484205a28a45cfaf96cecf&_m=0e696f637f954be98847e3a2286befc7&_e=W1luWzOEBEhb64rVso1It7RIDkdQAoapd3P_t_egX1M0Yk201A8bDG_mQGChBcYLN0XAq8FjmyIWZh8RHpoO3csOu6XK3DsbaPgnkT8aoU35865syXvANcDutJ9js7vPvZq2-7fRph-nVPEFLv332BFzVic78AUhp3zACekypKh87JVfhSJXjy7b7fIv92vwcgWf1xzBYaqxfQkZ8WkDcplsELKQ5z8m7yXkZHoFfXB6EPtQXz-Seyd4OGy9XSburKjcNCdJgndMuT8C2WRYx7Q9MqBCVd8hbHv-C-fUUgvnLVZp3EVzwETwrCYS2OsO4ZQTt66eQXu_JWNIdk9nRBWPZKMj4lQ5iuJxJc73TZlvvYFjEi8AxnKSkk64YdzDAQ-Y7jjjyy6RK1N2xDfsRU2rPMiesHlq_nXVRXvYkdc2My7FWrolWIYfHfz3oSNgNrxDwgDjkMcpm_l_sMjaWpS6xB9HJ67pm1U0H7isgKS6uRuEHrnHLLysgedNfFLKiC9h0DUtcuYdPAmFk094nqJoi92CEfzNF2qWpYAt-ttY2VU5Zk1YiMChM_R6Y82H)**

I continue to pray we can find a rally point of common sense, it was never going to be easy. Anybody pretending President Trump didn't open the door is being dishonest, anybody who can't bring themselves to question ANYTHING he decides has given up their citizenship. President Trump needs us to speak up and be ready to support some very tough decisions ahead, and it isn't a war in Iran, it's the constitutional crisis coming to secure elections in November. Or we will lose everything. Maybe nobody or not enough people really care anymore... That's the Greek tragedy. That's the 1984 orwellian doom! We deserve better, we can be better.

| | After a record _**thirteen**_**meet and greets** in the month of February as we prepared for caucus, March was even busier as caucus and assembly across all 21 counties got underway and we held a barrage of public events in the lead up. I was honored to attend many of the various caucuses and assemblies in person and even more via Zoom. When all was said and done, of the 168 delegates elected across the district, 143 delegates — **more than 85 percent** — were chosen by their peers to support me at tomorrow’s CD-4 assembly. I’m extremely proud of this, but I’m even more proud of the folks we engaged in the democratic process. **Over 900 people participated for the first time in caucus, over 100 veterans caucused for us, and 482 brand-new caucus goers were elected as delegates.**
I can’t let this month’s newsletter get sent without giving a **massive shoutout to the Eileen for Colorado team**. Both staff and volunteers. I’m merely one person, and the voter outreach, turnout and enthusiasm that our campaign felt through the caucus and assembly process is due directly to the unwavering dedication and countless hours or hard work my team put in. From thousands of swag deliveries to hundreds of hours on the phone, to the frankly obscene amounts of coffee consumed, this was a true team effort and I am beyond proud and grateful. Volunteers are truly the backbone of this campaign. Knocking on doors and engaging with neighbors goes such a long way when it comes from people in the community and I’m so grateful. This mobilization is just a taste of what we’re going to be able to bring to the general election and the how **we’re going to unseat Lauren Boebert once and for all — together with strategy and commitment**.
While my incredible team has putting in the hours in the office and in the district rallying voters, I’ve been continuing to hear from people all across the district and the thing that comes up the most is the lack of affordable healthcare in our district — particularly the rural communities. Throughout this campaign, I’ve committed to visiting as many rural hospitals as I can and in late February, I met with representatives of both **Keefe Memorial Hospital** and **Prowers Medical Center.** Prowers Medical Center, is a 25-bed critical access hospital that sees over 17,000 visits a year and serves patients from over four counties. Keefe Memorial Hospital serves nearly 1,800 square miles — a footprint roughly the size of Delaware — that includes all of Cheyenne County and into Western Kansas. We met with Claressa Millsap, the hospital’s CEO, who has found creative ways to fund the hospital amid fewer and fewer financial resources. Read more about her unique strategy from the [Colorado Sun](https://eileenforcolorado.us12.list-manage.com/track/click?u=400e8fa21dba23169b817268c&id=a7c8f32aaa&e=1c5f08419c).

Friend, this morning, when asked by the Supreme Court, the Solicitor General hesitated on whether Native Americans are birthright citizens.
Since he does not seem to understand basic American history (or the law), let me be clear: **Indigenous people are the original inhabitants of this continent, and here in New Mexico, we live that truth every day.**
The Solicitor General’s hesitation once again underscores that the Trump administration has never been concerned about the Constitution — for them, **it's all about exclusion and power.**

Trump has gutted Medicaid and SNAP benefits, attacked voting rights, and now wants to change our very Constitution to redefine who this country's citizens are.
**
This is a threat not only to New Mexicans but also to our nation's democracy and freedom.
**
With our rights on the line, governors are our best chance to serve as a backstop when the federal government abuses its power — _which is why the governor’s race here in New Mexico is so important_.
**I have gone up against Trump before and won, friend, which is why I know I have what it takes to stand up to this administration's attacks from day one. But I can't get there without you.**_[Please, will you rush $5 or whatever you can spare now to help me become governor of New Mexico and act as a brick wall against Trump?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/7306?refcode=jtk539-fr-nd&t=2&akid=8702%2E400544%2EnA8TmB)_

They want to erase everything we've built here and end our 32-year winning streak for the first time since 1994. We cannot let that happen. I'm proud to announce that Team McGuire has successfully passed two critical bills through the House in just three weeks.
The Wintergreen Emergency Egress Act This one is a massive win for public safety. For 25 years, this issue remained unsolved, with six different past congressional offices in the 5th attempting to find a fix. When my team and I learned of this issue in my district last August, we rolled up our sleeves and got to work. By working across the aisle and staying focused on results, we did the "impossible" and passed this bill through the House in just six months with bipartisan support.
The Make the District of Columbia Safe and Beautiful Act In addition to the Wintergreen Emergency Egress Act, my bill to revitalize and secure our nation's capital has officially passed. This bill codifies President Trumps Executive Order. Constituents from my district travel to DC everyday for work and leisure. We are committed to ensuring that the heart of our Republic, our nation's Capitol, is a safe, clean, and welcoming place for every American who visits.
The Bottom Line Results Matter: Whether it's a decades-old safety concern at Wintergreen or the safety of our people when they visit our capitol, we are proving that with the right work ethic and a commitment to working as a team for success, we can get Washington working again. Thank you for your continued support as we keep fighting for you!

clean_body: | | | | == == | 21 Days to Save Virginia | | | Join the Vote No Rally with Governor Youngkin & Congressman McGuire! 🇺🇸 Virginia is at a crossroads. Join us in Lynchburg to help us get out the vote. When: April 11, 2026 | 9:00 AM - 11:00 AM Where: Bella Rose, 1220 Graves Mill Rd, Lynchburg, VA Special Guest: Governor Glenn Youngkin Featured Speakers: Sen. Mark Peake, Sen. Luther Ciphers, and Del. Wendell Walker Get Involved: Learn the latest on redistricting and how you can help through door knocking, phone banking, or outreach. Supported by Turning Point Action and The Family Foundation. Make a plan to knock doors with us after the rally. Get involved, VOTE NO, and please tell a friend. If you want to join Team McGuire and help us help Trump Save America, please contact Ramona Christian at ramona@mcguireva.com or call her at 434 391 4546. | Huge News to Share! | I'm proud to announce that Team McGuire has successfully passed two critical bills through the House in just three weeks. The Wintergreen Emergency Egress Act This one is a massive win for public safety. For 25 years, this issue remained unsolved, with six different past congressional offices in the 5th attempting to find a fix. When my team and I learned of this issue in my district last August, we rolled up our sleeves and got to work. By working across the aisle and staying focused on results, we did the "impossible" and passed this bill through the House in just six months with bipartisan support. The Make the District of Columbia Safe and Beautiful Act In addition to the Wintergreen Emergency Egress Act, my bill to revitalize and secure our nation's capital has officially passed. This bill codifies President Trumps Executive Order. Constituents from my district travel to DC everyday for work and leisure. We are committed to ensuring that the heart of our Republic, our nation's Capitol, is a safe, clean, and welcoming place for every American who visits. The Bottom Line Results Matter: Whether it's a decades-old safety concern at Wintergreen or the safety of our people when they visit our capitol, we are proving that with the right work ethic and a commitment to working as a team for success, we can get Washington working again. Thank you for your continued support as we keep fighting for you! | | | We all know what happens when voters stay at home. The radical left is working overtime to redraw our maps and silence our conservative voices. Their agenda is clear: higher taxes, less safety, and the erosion of our 2nd Amendment rights. We are the only thing standing in their way. The Stakes: If these unfair maps pass on April 21, we risk losing Republican representation in this district for a generation. Our Progress: Signs and letters delivered. A growing army of volunteers. * Thousands of doors knocked. The Challenge: We cannot afford "bad actors" or internal infighting. We need a united front to get out the vote and protect our values. United We Stand, Divided We Fall. Will you help us cross the finish line? We are working hard to make Virginia's 5th District the best place to live, work, and raise your family in peace. Don't hesitate to reach out if we can be of help. In just fourteen months, through the grace of God, my team and I have achieved a ton of accomplishments. Here is some of what we have been up to: | Number One Priority Right Now, Vote NO Unfair Maps | | | | | Democrat Deceivers | | | Did you know democrats proposed over 50 new taxes in Richmond while at the same time voting themselves a huge pay raise? When they ran on affordability, obviously it was affordability for them, not We The People. | McGuire Endorsed By President Trump for Re-election | | | | | | McGuire Bill, Shall Not Be Infringed Act | | Gun-free zones make good people helpless victims. Our right to protect our families is absolute. That's why I introduced the Shall Not Be Infringed Act, which gives victims of violence in gun-free zones the power to sue the government. Also, Last week I spoke with President Trumps 2nd Amendment task force in DC to help formulate a plan to go after these unconstitutional gun laws coming out of Richmond. | McGuire Questions Bill and Hillary Clinton on Epstein | | | We questioned Bill and Hillary Clinton about the Unspeakable Evil in the Epstein files in New York. | | | Stephanie Reed Endorsement | | | "In the words of AG Jason Miyares, 'Councilwoman Stephanie Reed has proven herself to be a leader who follows through on her promises.' On the City Council, she has been a warrior for safer streets, responsible spending, and the values that Lynchburg families hold dear. As a Navy SEAL veteran, I know what real leadership looks like. I am proud of Stephanie and her veteran husband for their unwavering service to our local veteran community. She has earned my full endorsement for re-election. I urge you to join me in voting for Stephanie Reed in the Republican Primary. Like Jason Miyares said: 'She has delivered.' -Congressman John McGuire | Charlotte County GOP | | Really appreciate my time spent with you. Thank you for all you are doing to help the cause! I Voted For The Save America Act | | Did You Know, Even 17 Year Olds can Vote No? | | | Please spread the word, even 17 year olds can vote NO right now, if they will be 18 before the November 3rd election. | Children's Miracle Network | | These amazing people help raise money to support and save the lives of children with lefe threatening conditions. | | | Foster Fuels Well Represented in Lunenburg, VA | | | "Vote NO" Post Card Writing | | | Thank you Ramona Christian for hosting folks from several counties to sign write Vote NO messages on post cards. | We Support Our Logging Community | | | Logging is huge in Virginia, especially in Virginia's 5th Congressional district. My first bill as your congressman is a bill to support our farmers and our logging community. Thank you for all you do for jobs and to support Virgina's economy. | NRA Banquet Amherst County | | | Thank you to the NRA for letting me speak at your event in Amherst County, Virginia. I had an opportunity to talk about my "Shall Not Be Infringed Act", and some of the illegal and unconstitutional gun grab policies coming out of Richmond. Tracy and I were honored to sit with our friends Appomattox County Sheriff Robby Richardson and his wife Taylor. Thank you ==, ==, Delegate ==, and other legislators for fighting to protect our gun rights in Richmond. I also want to thank everyone who showed up tonight at the fundraiser to support the cause. | | | | | Patriots! | | | It's always great running into these patriots WRVA's == and former Delegate ==. Thanks for all you do! | Campbell County GOP | | | Thank you GOP Chair Sarah Lawson, Ann Parker, Claude Harris, and team for all you are doing! | RIP Brandon Shah | | | Sad Truth In Sarcasm | | | The US Senate must pass the Save America Act. | | | | Thank You Louisa County GOP | | | | | | | | | The American Spirit! | | | A Hero Runs to the Fight | | | Officers like NYPD Chief Aaron Edwards are why I have and will continue to support our men and women in law enforcement. Without them we would not have a country. | Thank You Goochland GOP | | | | | | | MAGA, Everyone Should Support A Great America! | | | | | Thank You Prince Edward GOP | | Thank You Danville GOP | | Amelia County | | | | | | | | | Thank You President Trump! | | Congressman Rob Wittman and David Botkins | | | Thank you for all you two are doing to help us get out the vote. Vote NO to Unfair maps! | | | American Veterans Vote | | | Great to run into my friend and fellow veteran COL Mike Flanagan USA (RETD) and his wife. | Amy Stewert Has a New Hanover Air BnB Business | | | | | | | Delta Star Has a Great Message | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | There were Zero Epstein files released during four years of Democrat Biden. President Trump and House Republicans have released over three million files in just fourteen months. Everything we read exonerates Trump and even shows Trump was the only one sounding the alarm about the evil of Epstein. We must protect the victims and prosecute the criminals. | | | Democrats Did This | | | Technology is Advancing | | A friend and fellow veteran (a US Marine) and his son made this super fast street legal car using 3d printing and additive manufacturing. He drove it from his garage to different race tracks, set five track records previously held by a four million dollar ferrari, and then drove it back home to his garage. | Doing Work Around The District | | | We need your prayers and advice. Raise your hand if you want your representative to work harder than anyone else. | National Prayer Breakfast in DC With Liberty University | | | | | Christians from all over the world gathered to pray in DC for the National Day of Prayer. We enjoyed speaking with Liberty University President and fellow veteran Dondi Costin and Thomas road Baptist Church Pastor Johnathan Falwell. | | Prince Edward GOP Chair Carolyn Bowman | | | RIP To Our Friend And Fellow Legislator Barry Knight | | | Barry Knight was the best! | Secretary Of War Pete Hegseth | | Making our military more lethal and the world safer! | | | | | | | | | | | We Must Pass The Save America Act | | | Why We Need My Federal Accountability Felony Obstruction Bill (FAFO) | | | | | | | | | | | Nick Name For Getting Results | | | Helping Folks Get Home | == | This was a very nice video sent to me by a constituent for helping a young man get home from Israel back in June during the Twelve- Day-War with Iran. We worked with the State Department and Department of War to assist 57 more constituents return home from Israel today! == | I Voted "No" to Unfair Maps | | | I voted NO to unfair maps on the first day of early voting. Don't let politicians you will never meet in northern Virginia take away your voice. These crooks clearly violated our constitution and they are trying to steal Virginia. This is calculated deception. Democrats are trying to trick you with misleading words on the ballot, billboards, and more. Don't let your family members and friends fall for it. Please get your friends to vote NO early at the registrar office in the county or city they live. If you will be 18 years old before the November election, you can register and then vote NO to these unfair maps. The last day to vote NO is April 21. 25 Year Success at Wintergreen | == My bill to create an emergency egress at Wintergreen Ski Resort passed the House. According to the Fire Chief, Curtis Sheets, he has worked with many congressmen on this issue over the last 25 years with no result. Based on that past, he was skeptical it could be done. When the Fire Chief told me about this issue at a site visit back in August, my incredible team got to work and I built bridges needed to get it done in the US Senate and the House. By the grace of God we passed the bill. A highlight for me was bringing the Fire Chief to D.C. to testify on this issue. It really is amazing what we can achieve when we work as a team. We will keep you posted! If you have facebook, click this link to listen to the Wintergreen Fire Chief talk about this success. == | Are You Sick of the Fraud? | | == | We questioned failed Governor Tim Walz, a man who abandoned his troops right before they deployed to combat. We asked him about the the 9 billion dollar fraud, whistleblower intimidation, and more. One constituent said "I don't know if I'm paying taxes or paying criminals." == | Vote Ramona Christian Next VA 05 Committee Chair | | | Ramona Christian holds a degree in political science and has been a steadfast leader in the conservative movement. She served on Donald Trump's platform team, was one of just three Fifth District delegates selected to represent President Trump at the Republican National Convention, and she played a key role on the Trump Virginia campaign team, helping organize Trump rallies across the Commonwealth last year. She also serves as Political Director for Congressman John McGuire and she currently serves as the Buckingham County GOP Chair. Ramona is a no-nonsense leader, a trusted friend, and someone who absolutely will get things done. She has my complete and total endorsement for Virginia's 5th Congressional District Committee Chair. To learn more including how to vote for her and to join her team, email Ramona at ramonachristian862@gmail.com | I Love CVille Podcast | | == | I Love CVille with Jerry Miller. Thank you for having me on your show. We've received a lot of great feedback! | Helping Our Veterans | == We were successful in helping a fellow veteran from my district get his daughter Savali to a place where she could receive life saving treatment. "Sylvester Craft said that after McGuire got involved, the VA agreed to pay the entire bill. He said they were waiting for transportation to Stanford." Savali Craft is a mother of two and an Air Force veteran. She is not out of the woods yet and still needs your prayers. Please spread the word. | If you want to join Team McGuire and help us help Trump Save America, please contact Ramona Christian at ramona@mcguireva.com or call her at 434 391 4546. | For God and Country, | Congressman John McGuire VA 05 Soli Deo Gloria Jesus is my Savior Husband Father Navy SEAL Business Owner -Trump Endorsed -NRA Endorsed -Susan B. ## Artemis II Sends Crew Toward the Moon
NASA launched four astronauts [toward the moon](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL1urDAQhZ_GdKDxrMFL4eI2dHvblMjgMUxk8Mr2gvbtI5K8QZrRNOfnOx-P8WE58L78txuZ4uO405kDlUJptKnQxpk52Nc-rz4myiVTOkYE7GpQNeDoLIf3qCpnPBHSrSIjtW4lqvYO1Wq8ouneza6VTnXTnabWay373ipwrfK-YnO5gQKUAP1NN1L3gGqyKGfoJjkLBeS4xNR8Rt7LSj6840GpmeNWBbOW8szi9k_gIHA4z7PZbbbNEg-BwxTikgUOG-fMcb_eK03gAOo6UuAQ-KD6l7Vmrn9oa2ff9evpbKFLVSXjnieHwLnTQsGyWQ7fDcqfZjsMfgUAAP__4RSAfQ) Wednesday evening, the first crewed deep-space flight in more than 50 years. The Artemis II crew lifted off from Kennedy Space Center at 6:35 p.m. ET aboard the Space Launch System rocket, generating 8.8 million pounds of thrust. Commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, mission specialist Christina Koch, and Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen are on an approximately 10-day trip around the moon and back. [Watch the liftoff here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFuwyAUgOHT4C3W45kYMzB0iLc0Y0eE8SOmwiYCEte3r9IrdP6lb_i_ruZqQwzb_dOupKtPZqO9RKqVsrG50hpKCNE-N7f4lKnUQvllELA_gTgBmtmGeBjRzNoTIXUNaS7lmaM4D9AsWjkpZummHginzs0I3PfKK6skDsO5a4J-ayAAOYDqZMulAhSTRe6gn7hjAmgONeX2O4WtLuTjkV6UW5fWJuql1kdh3QfDkeG473t7pGd9TvTuDMeypFwLw_FH3WI2l9tlEE3W82MPMYbSSybgvtoQ_7z6rwkvjb8BAAD__9accDk). The crew could travel farther from Earth than any humans in history, potentially [breaking the record](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpDAQRL8GMqOmMXAOHFxCNpdeiBpoD70y9sj2DJq_X7G7f7BRlVRSlV79v803Ei_h_o8OtsXFOfCZPZfCaaZU-JAs4ukZ1t3FxLlkTq8ZAQcFWgHOG4l_z7rerGNG7mq27Tj2Ler-D9S71WSMg8WA7sbe9aZfqCMcOz0YROx0LfZqAw3YAphubNrRAOqFsF1hWNq10sCblJiajyih7Oz8O744NWs8am_3Uh656v5WOFU4nefZrEu-KK68wumyl1Am9UOkRNQRY1DfYIpySTHQs2TlvNz3oh6eQoVTnez2OMV7ycNYabgfJP5rt_zqrJfFzwAAAP__Nxl-4Q) of about 248,655 miles set by Apollo 13 in 1970. The mission will test life-support systems and critical operations in deep space, paving the way for future lunar landings and eventual [crewed missions to Mars](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D9urDAQgPHTmA40Hsy_wsVr6Pa1KdEsHpaJjL2yvaC9fZQoN8gFftL3fdyWG4mX8PhPB9uyxSXwlT2XwmmhVPiQLOLpFdZ9i4lzyZzOBQH7GkwNuDgS_15M5ezGjNxWbPUwdBpNN0K1297AeHcj9tvYaQ3tOE0IBM5hh7prqRL7rYEB1ABTOzR6mADNnVCv0N_1qgywkxJT8xkllJ03_44np2aNR-XtXsozq_afwlnhfF1XEyhT84inwnl_HRRyLaHOT1pZ4fwbpXCuknXPS7yX3A_KwOMg8T9o-dOJ0-JXAAAA__9BNnE4).
## Trump Vows to End Iran War in Weeks
President Trump opened his [primetime address](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGuozAQRb8GOqPxYOBRuNgm3dt2SzTAEGZj7MiegPL3q-wvvP7qHp3z53v6JgkS77_pYK9bmiJfJbAq54my8iFFJNArLvuWMhctnM8JAXsDzgBOK0l4T65e_caM3Nbs7TB0Fl33BfXuebGE-EVzO4-AI_SENKLbxrm3ywiuFv95AwdoAcZ2aOwwArqZ0C7Qz3apHPAqmnLzN0nUnbfwTifnZklHHfyu-ixV-6vCW4W367qaj8LF_PgMKrxJpmguyibIyUbz63gaTYbWNXMpJpJKiqZolgcXs6SoEl9srB36vrNdnf36vCQEKf1QObgfJOE_W38U7PT4LwAA___STICB) to the nation Wednesday night by congratulating the Artemis II astronauts, who lifted off hours earlier on the first crewed moon mission in over 50 years. _"God bless those four unbelievable astronauts,"_ he said. Trump then turned to the war, saying military objectives against Iran are "nearing completion" and vowing to bomb the regime ["back to the stone ages"](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD0SmzAQhU8juvWIRUamUJGGzmlTMkIsRomQGGmxze0zyhXSbLPzvvfz6zk9rQ8-vn7anQyvaYr0KYGYKU82M-2-eB_sGd22pkyFC-X3hBJ7kAokTov14ZpUs5iVCKlryLRa31tU94dsNoMP1BoH1HZWK7p1oX7tHw6XmdzdzkPjTaVJJbGVcuj0rdWDRDVbbJ3s59YJJWnxnPLtd_KRN1rDld6Uby7tTTAb81FE90PgKHCM15EK15fAsYIFjlLV0woczwK1n8CR87kfYGNMZ3RUwGcb4eNDgJlg8wz05Uw7hQs2mxeohsAbQaQvA0IHH6I_ldRksxxV6UuvhZKv3frwLxv_16Bvg38DAAD__4-piig) over the next two to three weeks. Trump called the surge in gas prices "short term" and blamed it entirely on Iranian attacks on oil tankers, promising prices would "rapidly come back down" once the war ends. Iran denied seeking a ceasefire and said the Strait of Hormuz would remain closed. Trump said the waterway "will open up naturally" because Iran will need to sell oil to rebuild. [Watch the full address here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGO6yAQheGnwV2sYYxNUlDcxl1uuyXCMMSzwiYC1t68_Sr7Clsf6ZPO_3G3d8eJ98d_t5FpMdudzpqoNSrWlUYbV-bkvna_xlyotkrlsAg4XUBdAG1wnF5WdcFEIqShIyO1HiWq8QrdanAhra8wuBiChwALjhimcZFej-Dl0LF5a6AAJcBt0L3UN0C1OJQepkV6oYACt1z6z8x7WymmVz6o9D5vXTJra88qhn8CZ4HzeZ59zN_vF-9d4HxwoCxwnoYbKoCrBCmxKyY8T06J66SFgsfmOP2C7U8VDoM_AQAA__--Hm72).
## Trump Signs Order Restricting Mail-in Voting
President Trump has issued an [executive order restricting](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFvgzAQBeBfYzbQ-XBCPHjowpauHZGBc7jK2JG5QPPvK_oXOj-970nv6z7cPUdOj0-_kpOQh0THFkmEyuCL0Mobc_SvNC0hF9pko7IPCHitwdSAw-w5vgdTzS4QIbUVOd11F43mcoNqceSNtkFbq-dwGb1pjbY02lsA9H4OtmJ3amAANYBtu0Z3FtCMHvUE11FPygDNLLk035mTLBTiO-9UmimvVXSLyHNT7YfCXmF_HEczpXE6Q4X9SSvsoVXYt1phL-W1PuvVc6w51XsWTo-afmh6Ce9U5zJTaRZZY1Xc_Dw4Rt6unTLwODt_k_Kvn3aHvwEAAP__lEN76w) mail-in voting ahead of November's midterm elections. The order directs the Department of Homeland Security to compile lists of verified citizens in each state and instructs the Postal Service to [deliver ballots only](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OqzAQhZ_GdETjwUAoXNyGLrfdEhk8xLMyOLInZPP2K_IKW58_ne_rNt0cR97v_91GVtY07fQqkUQoTy4LbVyYo3vuS1hTpiKF8jEhYFeDqQEn7zi-J1N5uxIhNRVZ3fetRtNeoQrWwdIP7Qq6a83V6E7T3PS-ITQewRBVbM82MIAaYGj6i-4HQDM71At0s16UAfIsKV--E-8SaI3vdFC-LGmrog0ij6KafwpHhaMEChzjqSkcQ9roPKRwdH7jnYtkJ5x2hWN7hWFosaYfWp7CB9Upe8r19gFSzy7GJGeyytY_Xhwjl65XBu6n4zMufyJ2WPwNAAD__61ngB8) to voters on those approved lists. Legal experts say the order is almost certain to face [court challenges](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDHOnDAQRk9jOiN78AJbUKSh-9OmRMYeLxMZG9mzkD-nj9grpB69-fTer6_ly1Kk9Pppd5w45CXhVSMyY1lsYdypEkX7Tm4LuWDliuVcQEEvlZEKFm8pfi-m8VNABOwanPQwPDSYx6iaber02HeDGzGsz2HtjQoPMMbroMfggsWGpvubMgq0Us9uaPXwVGBWC9qpftVOGIWeOJf2d6bEG4b4nU8srct7E6eN-aii-yFgFjBf19WemXFFy20uLwFzskw52ShgvpcEzKoTMHdawOzvg5dc3vshP1Y7ecayS4zobk7iH3RvphNlLh6LtGvFxIhytxTlamPMXOWRK9so7zrkUDpi-oupbnTISJUFzE2Z_HFRjFT7QRj1uvmPA_9X-HOCfwEAAP__wXmZ1g), since the Constitution gives states and Congress authority over elections. A similar order from last year was largely blocked by judges. The order follows months of pressure on Congress to pass the SAVE America Act, which would require voters to present a photo ID and proof of citizenship. The House passed the measure in February, but it has stalled in the Senate.

## Man Indicted in 'Killing Fields' Murders
A Galveston County grand jury [indicted](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGymzAQRb8GOnlWa4FMoSIN3UubklmkBZQI5JGEMX-f4Tl_kHr3nrnn_voavsgHv80_aWVT3lMcNj5y4FI4DX98uG6T5-Cy35y3ZeWtrDQgYCtACcDBkQ_noGpnRnCdrNlIrRuJWj9UvZgOLI7QdZYQuLEoqdWauO2gkRKhqb25YKAApYQ74O1uH9o-CDSokRoaKwXsfInpVhYu_KY8hTO-ON1sXOtgllKeubr_qLCvsD-O4zbFN7ZL3HOJ2_VUYX9ZVdh_x8U_L_ERE3nPT7ZFfAzZCYXiZEpZBCqcxEzhxRdL2Lhv5RRzos2J33s662Tc87hwudWVgnklH757lf9b82XwbwAAAP__tASMeA) 61-year-old James Dolphs Elmore Jr. of Bacliff for his alleged role in the murders of two women whose bodies were discovered in the 1980s in an undeveloped area of League City. Since the 1970s, over 30 bodies [have been discovered](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDGypCAQQE-DGRa2CBgQbGL2N93QaqAZqY_6C5lx5vZbzuwNNux61a_69Z-v-QtTTtvtN65k6zPu80bnkalWKvN3yheLiXI40haSryttdcUZBCguJBcwB0z5NcsmWCfC2DVkO62HDrQ2slmsjjiOYzCDgaCk0h5JuODV0DvnUKom2UsmpICuE72AtvdGe4NCC-lwQMekoJDqXtq6UKUnHjG_9geV1u9rk-1S68_B-l8MJgbTeZ7t97LfL8hgwlKTz8RguroYTHn3mD8jx1LoqPzt5P9i-aeWZ8LbnbhP9cXXewlUrm0wA1cjQewkck8SuIwSuEEnuDI6BopD6E3fFBt-zst4KM2kuK2Y8vve-n9fflj4GwAA___9l5DZ) along I-45 between Houston and Galveston, a region that came to be known as the Texas Killing Fields. Laura Miller, 16, [disappeared](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO4yAQhp8Gd0TDmBhcUFzjbq-90hrDeIMCYYVxvHn7k3P3Blt_0jfz_X8-5g-KKT4-f1Nm177XMj_42BK3xnW-x3SyNXIKW3yE6FvmR8s0I-AgQUvAOVBMr1l3wS0QRtWxU8ZcFRpjdXdzC9CojEGlNI0LWrbECw8EnvveD30X3SkDDagU9ICX3lvjLYEBvdCVFqGBQ2ylXtqNG3_TtqZXeXK9-JK75G6tfW2i_yVwEjgdx3G538p-QoET1RZ9YoHT2SVwSsVTEji9RfJ_ofyXKPNeA1f5jL7FvEnaQ-WX9KXcZaK9kswxJa4CJ7RXaVmPHnGVbIGlXs0gbRgHCdYu2psVgr121YWv47yyDUZo-MwU0_vx9rO5nw7_BgAA___3g5PF) in September 1984, while Audrey Cook, 30, vanished in December 1985. Miller's father founded Texas EquuSearch, a nonprofit that helps families find missing loved ones. Clyde Hedrick, 72, long a prime suspect in the deaths of the two women, killed himself last month before prosecutors could present new evidence to a grand jury. However, they secured indictments for manslaughter and evidence tampering against Elmore, who allegedly [prepared](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2O2zAQhuHTUN0Y_LNlFSrcqNsgRYAF0ggUObQGIakFObbWtw-0yQ22_oB38Mz72_zmKFG5_3AZR_6M21xwbwmZsc5_KB1bJEyhUQnkOWPh7GYt9QWkBann4Ci9ZtuFcZFhUB2Oqu_PSvf91XbriF5djYl6sBdjzUXJOEQfzaCWwcjgdUfjEZNWaqWkkfpk_LX3Vyd7aRd3douwEgPxVk-8IuOnazG9tifWk99yl8aV-aMJcxN6Enra9_2UWzk2oScs8GhCTwdK6MlXyij0lF0Bv7p6xwBU4CsK_7Xwjwv5UQPWBm173FeG7cHwJM-UG0THK1ZgypApJazwQlcbLBi3iuBqxcZCT67C7aZ-v59__urqGD7240K79MLKe3aUvgD8vbc_R_03AAD__8d0mhM) a "vial of cocaine" for Hedrick to give to Miller. Galveston County District Attorney Kenneth Cusick [said](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDGO4zAMRU8jdwwkWrE8hYtt3M22Wxq0xCTCylIgcZzx7RcO9gZTP5D_v__nc_mkmGK-_6aNJ_m-lSXzqyUW4br8jelkt8gptJhD9LJxlo0W1DiAtqBxCRTTsdguTKsOH6bjyTh3NejcaLvH5AyawaAd_DjyOqz9dejdhw3j6hAH33dxOp9pq9EY3Wu89H50fiTttF3pSquymkOUUi_yYOFvard0lJ3rxZetS9ND5NlU_0vhrHCm1Zv-JArnZ2micH7fwH-ZBm8d8NQY7pR2blIy-PKV5YBA0OgAqgxFHlyBvMSdITGFBi_OAl-5lbRzgK1UBqvhYKpN4WzGEdENqHDu6hSerzOwDU5Zfd8opndd-dnI-4T_AgAA___RU5Ff) there are "other active leads in the case" but declined to provide further details. "_We got other girls to find, we got closure to bring more families_ ," said Tim Miller.
## Judge Rejects Suit Challenging IRS Rule
Judge Cam Barker of the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Texas has dismissed a lawsuit challenging the Johnson Amendment, a tax code provision that bars churches and other nonprofits from [endorsing candidates](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLFug0AQRL8GOtCynDkorkhD57Qp0XK3mE0OsLi1sf8-Ir-QbqQnjWbe13W4kkRZb5-0sNPXtA0rHymyKu_Dj8STTcIxJFmDeF141YUGBGwKMAXgEEjiezB5cCOErsrZVdZeKrS2NfnsvAnjWDW26TobEME3XW0nf8HWWO4IcnFnGRjAqoIasKx9a31LYMGMdKExM8BBdNtLnVn5RWmK7-3Je-m3JY9uVr2nrP7IsM-wP46jfNO8bSfNsD_vZNjTruIjn3HiwDvF4vsRblwESYukxKnw82P3M6ci0pEeogUAmgob6MpZl5jvLtyP00hqbGbgtpDEvwn6P3FPh78BAAD___Ofgww) for elected office. The lawsuit, filed in 2024 by two Texas churches and the National Religious Broadcasters, argued the law inhibits free speech and religious liberty. While the Biden administration sought to dismiss the lawsuit, the Trump administration [sided with the plaintiffs](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDuu4zAMAE8jdzIk-iOnULGNu2y7pUFLdKxE_sBi4uT2CwV4J3j1gENy_l2HK4YY1ttfXMjye9qGlc4UiZmO4RFiZlOg6FNYfXC80MoLDqCglaqWCgaPIX6GuvB2VP6iC7LamEaDMV1dzFY757vJqY68JnVpoG3Q0Yj-AthORhfBZpmqFWitKgVl5TrjOlRG1SM2OIpakQ-8HSXPxPTGNMXP9qKjdNtSRDsz70lUfwT0AvrzPMtHQs5QQJ-_EdB_xwT0eZWAXlUC-kr_AHl_-hvJg-7kOMn9mWbJm4zE0s3Pw82U5IIPkvsWAweHUdLqtyNRzpG9xWH9fuZcqTWiVrcFQ_zex7-r-rLwPwAA__92GI1K) and proposed an agreement in which the IRS would not enforce the 1954 statute. In his Tuesday ruling, Barker, a 2019 Trump appointee, said courts are barred from "providing declaratory relief with respect to federal taxes," suggesting the Johnson Amendment [could be challenged](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO2zAMQL9G3hRItBM5g4Yu3q5rR4OWaIepLAUSe3f5-0L9hW4EHvFAvl8f6wdy4nz8xJO8fO9lzfTVEolQXX9z6mxnSrFxjhzkpCwnrmDgps2kDawROb3XaYh-M_FuB_LWuasF5-ZpePg7WArWORvxinaG6_1232cEHOM-2nEb2HeZmQxYa0YDlzHMLsxonJk2vOKmJkORpdSLPEjoG9ue3uWT6iWUc0j-IfJqavyhYFGwVEp8cMn9jb6gYOl-BYsZFSyjVbBsmHXJ-oVNSm2aciy1cT50wBw5opCudCLnpjnrV8JAGnehqp9_4tHhk4I0_SyP3ErWeFKOvYxuJJKojwqWofr4-uoN282pyRwncvp3tPxf6k8PfwMAAP__9rqVRQ) if churches actually lost their tax-exempt status for engaging in political activity. An attorney for the plaintiffs [promised to appeal](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOozAQhJ8GOiOzGBsKF9fQ5dor0dpegnMGInsTkrc_ca_wdyN90ozm-3ObbxhT3O-_cSPLn-WYdzpLImbK89-YLrZESqHEPUTPG-284QwStJBKSJgDxvSdVR2sk2Fsa7KtMX0LxgyqXi0Zr5zrzAgtak2uGwB75xfnNchRQx3tVSaVhLaVnYSm84PxA0ojlcMeXaUkhchHbnglpg-WJX2PN-XGH1ud7Mr8LFX3q4Kpguk8z-aL63FctILpulPBhJmjT3TFVxGPV7iTyPQgz0XEXMQTPQvooO9HGHSz8pbqbMPzvBQUbSol7xvG9H-Tf2bqbeFfAAAA__-FL31i) the decision, calling it "an error." A statement from Americans United for the Separation of Church and State, however, praised the ruling: "Tax-free giving to charities should fund charitable work, not partisan politics."
## Houston Astronaut Pilots Artemis II

Dear Fellow Patriot,

January 6th was 5 years ago...

...but for many J6 prisoners, _**their nightmare is still ongoing.**_

Despite receiving a pardon from President Trump, these **unjustly jailed men and women are still struggling to rebuild their lives** after 4 years behind bars.

Like Damon Beckley.

After four years as a political prisoner, **Damon came home to a life that had been completely destroyed.**

His family's landlord evicted them from their home, forcing his wife and son to live in an apartment with no heat. And Damon's health collapsed in prison after contracting MRSA and later requiring emergency cancer surgery.

To make matters worse, **Damon, his wife, and their son are now facing eviction and possible homelessness again.**

Sadly, Damon's story is far too common among J6 prisoners.

In just the last 60 days, [Stand in the Gap has received over $60,000 in urgent pleas](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=8949081cb98444faa3a57db6ff8e2830&_e=zlmloVuN2cbKttdnBf5DHzmENptOLd3KLU-JbA50801MO5rxU0ipvt89oaCc5gFBpfSAsfM3Q6ZwAol6Cg0muQK-PdavMJmpYQl-tQggGk6SFBw_bWKtPKlIh4etqNV344XhgNxd8xv3nPSeDTT8GA6GjsFfx-tLzhZTU2Dt47W4nLZXx6X7qVRB7aeHuhe-Lzmi24yE8bQwrOANGS6nfwq9wDHXK4v3lRGbZOxhVXxR-sHM_ZJhXEAs4PrhEYHudUQ4TXcBHQjmkZwsLM9Q6hUaOw8tyWkjl-ZOAPC_N4qX9K4-sT7SDM3us-19d5FOr9FV6hV8JERGeygVmQHFQlPlRAwpBO1-iX55eDjlZIhG8BrwZswdq7CJsFMrwdRzBReeudI4o000G0vlUhy-KeSYKX3saVS_M3WSHxfZ85bJWPX6-V9_rMNfSzvFNxnrJpdFHR2AtTj4KOW2Cvq4unvNXRUHZdN_1x-dTdI0WhhCNcYJbHzePPqp85NxG59jOsAZa_KLZD4hojG-Bwbg64epUkYpNxv7LGk1z12A5DfAMuTUkrveoGKyZy1eZF659r6VeygkHiijQM1CX8VGMusBi8Jxmke0O9eneLSPlJmzf9Exl4ASYTZQHdzw8ncXqbwKk0xTLfifyHbKjrzlRg%3D%3D) for help from January 6 families struggling to survive.

**Unless we can count on your help, we 'll be forced to TURN AWAY some of these desperate families.**

clean_body: Dear Fellow Patriot, January 6th was 5 years ago... ...but for many J6 prisoners, their nightmare is still ongoing. Despite receiving a pardon from President Trump, these unjustly jailed men and women are still struggling to rebuild their lives after 4 years behind bars. Like Damon Beckley. After four years as a political prisoner, Damon came home to a life that had been completely destroyed. His family's landlord evicted them from their home, forcing his wife and son to live in an apartment with no heat. And Damon's health collapsed in prison after contracting MRSA and later requiring emergency cancer surgery. To make matters worse, Damon, his wife, and their son are now facing eviction and possible homelessness again. Sadly, Damon's story is far too common among J6 prisoners. In just the last 60 days, for help from January 6 families struggling to survive. Unless we can count on your help, we 'll be forced to TURN AWAY some of these desperate families. Like I said, Fellow Patriot... Damon's story is all too common. We recently received a request from Kirstyn Niemela, who spent months living in a camper in a friend's backyard during the freezing New Hampshire winter. Because of the stigma of being labeled a J6er, she has struggled to find stable employment. Now, with odd jobs having dried up during the winter months, she's at risk of losing the truck she depends on for transportation and work. Then there's Benjamen Burlew, who is now two months behind on his mortgage and electric bill after health issues wiped out the family's savings. If they fall any further behind, they could lose the home their children have lived in for 17 years. Five years ago, Damon, Kirstyn, and Benjamen were no different than you or me. They had steady jobs. Loving families. Homes they were proud of. And they believed in President Trump's vision for this nation. But the Far-Left turned them into political prisoners ... because they couldn 't jail all of us. Now these patriots are trying to rebuild their lives from nothing... and many of them simply can't do it alone. Stand in the Gap is their lifeline. That's why Stand in the Gap exists: to provide emergency financial aid, housing assistance, legal support, and medical help to the men and women who sacrificed everything. But we can only respond to these urgent requests with support from patriots like you, Fellow Patriot. Your support helps provide: Emergency financial aid to prevent homelessness Legal defense funds for ongoing civil lawsuits Medical support for J6ers suffering lasting health problems Basic living expenses while families rebuild their lives January 6th is NOT ancient history, Fellow Patriot. For these families, it's a nightmare they're still trying to escape. Without our urgent help, many of them will NOT survive to the next chapter. Stand in the Gap is their LAST lifeline... and that lifeline exists SOLELY because of generous supporters like you. Dear Peter, The culture is loud. But this month, the Church got louder. Honest and unapologetic conversations ignited in churches and on college campuses across the country — conversations that refuse to shrink back from truth. Churches hosted packed Christ and Culture Nights, where believers gathered to tackle today’s toughest issues with biblical truth and confidence. At the same time, our Pick Up the Mic events hit college campuses, creating spaces for students to ask hard questions and hear honest, Scripture-rooted answers. The first Pick Up the Mic stop of 2026 at Middle Tennessee State University featured Pastor Lucas Miles and Steve Deace, who discussed issues like immigration, Islam, paganism, and science. Students wanted the truth of God’s Word — this is what drives our mission.

Dear Friends and Neighbors,
I'm sure many of you have seen, if not experienced, the incredibly long lines at the airports. For weeks now, since Republicans shut down DHS, I have worked alongside my colleagues to fund TSA, FEMA, the Coast Guard, and more. I was clear we could do that without sending another penny to ICE. Last week, Republicans in the Senate agreed, and a motion was passed to fund DHS again. Now, Republicans in the House are stalling. It's unacceptable, and I will continue to fight to get workers paid.
**The So-Called "SAVE" Act** While it did not pass the Senate last week, House Republicans have said they still intend to impose their voter suppression bill on the American people. It's unfortunate that we are still debating the merits of the so-called SAVE America Act. Right now, Americans are struggling with the rising costs of housing, health care, gas, groceries, and more. The American people are suffering from the effects of a trade war started by this Administration and watching as we're stuck in an illegal and poorly planned war in Iran.
This affordability crisis demands an urgent resolution. Unfortunately, we have an Administration that is completely out of touch. There are so many real issues that we could be working on that would benefit the lives of working families across the country. But instead, the President has created a fantasy crisis and is committed to finding a solution to a problem that doesn't exist.
Reality says that noncitizen voting in federal elections is already against the law, and there are enforcement mechanisms in place. That is the law, and it should be followed. My colleagues on the other side of the aisle have claimed this bill is a commonsense election integrity measure focused on proof of citizenship, voter ID, and cleaner voter rolls. Reality says that on top of everything else people are dealing with right now, requiring even more paperwork would create real problems for so many people - like married women whose documents don't match because they changed their names to match their husbands', or members of our military who move locations often in service of their country. It would be a problem for people who rely on mail registration or absentee voting. It would be an undue burden for our seniors, veterans, students, and rural voters.
Voting already requires a form of American identification. My colleagues on the other side of the aisle say this bill would provide necessary aggressive voter-roll verification and removal of noncitizens from the rolls. Reality says this aggressive federal overreach would include requiring states to submit voter data to DHS - the same agency that is currently sending ICE goon squads of masked men to kill Americans in our streets. States would be required to submit their complete statewide voter registration lists to DHS for comparison through the SAVE program on an ongoing basis. That's completely impractical. The SAVE program was not designed to be a voter registration system, and it predictably has resulted in false matches and false ineligibility flags.
What's more, it gives DHS a continuing role in federal elections that it's not equipped or designed to handle. It hands over critical information to an Administration that has already proven it can't or won't keep the sensitive data of the American people protected. It hands over information to an Administration that has already failed its test of using its power for retribution.

Reality says this is being treated as an emergency right now because it's part of a broader electoral strategy that this Administration needs to be in place ahead of the upcoming midterm elections. People are unhappy with the direction we're going. They're upset that their government isn't working on the real issues they're facing. And instead of addressing the affordability crisis that's staring us in the face - the affordability crisis caused by this President- this Administration wants to guarantee a successful midterm election by "fixing" an electoral system that isn't broken.

The President already issued an Executive Order directing federal agencies to be more involved in election-related enforcement and citizenship verification. And since then, the DOJ has sought extensive voter data from nearly every state. At least 48 states and DC have received requests for their complete voter registration lists, and the DOJ has sued DC and 29 states, including Maryland, for refusing to provide statewide voter lists with driver's license and Social Security information. And this Administration is counting on Republicans in Congress to sell their fantasy. But reality has refuted every fantasy claim made in support of this bill. So, what are the architects of this bill actually seeking?
Simply put, they're seeking to suppress the vote. This is not a standard voter ID bill. This bill is not about protecting democracy. Protecting democracy would eliminate barriers that keep more Americans from voting. This bill doesn't do that. It does the opposite. This bill is a blatant attempt to kick eligible voters off the rolls and make it more complicated for Americans to register and vote.
States have already done an excellent job fashioning a system that works. The fantasy world this bill envisions would disrupt the way voter registration and voting actually work in practice. It would undermine or severely limit online registration, registration by mail, motor-voter systems, same-day registration, and voter registration drives by requiring in-person presentation of documentary proof. It would alter registration, list maintenance, and ballot-casting all at once, forcing states and election officials to rework systems that voters already rely on.
Maryland has worked hard to build a system that is both secure and accessible. This bill would undermine the progress that we and so many other states have made by replacing those successful, efficient state systems with new federal mandates and new legal risks for election officials. It would result in wrongful removals from voter rolls and more undue burdens, putting new barriers between eligible Americans and the ballot box.
If the President and my colleagues on the other side of the aisle want to ignore the urgent crisis facing the nation in order to fix issues with voting that actually do exist, they would endorse the bill that I introduced, the **Deceptive Practices and Voter Intimidation Prevention Act** , that would criminalize knowingly spreading false information about the time, place, or manner of voting, or about voter qualifications, and would prohibit threatening or coercing individuals not to vote or to vote a certain way. They would sign on to the numerous bills by my colleagues that I have cosponsored, like Senator Klobuchar's **Register America to Vote Act** that would automatically register all eligible citizens to vote when they turn 18. They would sign on to Senator Wyden's **Vote at Home Act** that would expand vote by mail, a method that has proven to increase voter participation. They would sign on to Senator Padilla's **Voter Purge Protection Act** that would prohibit states from using questionable voter purge tactics to take tens of thousands of eligible voters off the voting rolls.
You don't save America by silencing the voices of Americans. You save America by embracing the ideals that set us apart to begin with. The reality is that we should be encouraging more people to take full advantage of their rights. That's why we should be making it easier for eligible citizens to participate in our democracy, not harder. When a bill takes a fundamental right and wraps it in paperwork, penalties, and confusion, that is not election security. That is a step backward for American democracy.

And that's not what the American people want. They didn't ask for an additional crisis to deal with. The Administration has insisted on ignoring their calls for help on the affordability crisis. I will continue to raise my voice on behalf of all Marylanders, speaking out [at every turn against the SAVE Act](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15517.17616517.6049417.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fx.com%2fSen_Alsobrooks%2fstatus%2f2035408312808718485%3fs%3d20&redir_log=05470499502361). I ask that you continue to speak out alongside me.

**Fighting Through Legislation** It has been a busy two weeks in the Senate, and I continue fighting to introduce legislation that will help Maryland families. From extending WIC for new moms, to suicide prevention among our young people to workforce development, I believe these pieces of legislation will help our loved ones thrive and help create prosperous, healthy communities.

Legislation I introduced:

Extending WIC for New Moms Act: This bill would expand eligibility and support mothers and infants into the postpartum and breastfeeding periods through the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) programs. This legislation extends WIC eligibility in the postpartum period from 6 months to 24 months and in the breastfeeding period from 12 months to 24 months.

Legislation I cosponsored:

Social Determinants for Moms Act: This bill would establish a whole-of-government task force to address the United States Maternal Health Crisis. This legislation will also establish a Social Determinants of Maternal Health Fund to provide robust, sustained funding for community-based organizations, Indian Tribes and Tribal organizations, Urban Indian organizations, and public health departments to address social determinants of health during and after pregnancy - including housing, transportation, nutrition, environmental conditions, and other local needs.

Child Suicide Prevention Act: This bill would authorize the Department of Health and Human Services to award grants to health care providers, states, and schools to implement evidence-based suicide prevention programs, training, and curricula for individuals under age 26. It authorizes $30,000,000 in total funding for fiscal years 2027 through 2030, including $20,000,000 for health care-based programs and $10,000,000 for training and education initiatives.

Main Street Depositor Protection Act: This bipartisan legislation would require a data-driven process to increase deposit insurance coverage levels for business checking accounts at most banks and credit unions.

Delaware River Basin Reauthorization Act: This bill would amend the definition of the Basin's coverage to include Maryland, and it authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to give funding priority to projects serving a small, rural, or disadvantaged community. It re-authorizes the program to expire at the end of FY 2032.

National Transit Workforce Training Act: This bill would codify the Transit Workforce Center (TWC) to support recruitment, training, and retention of public transportation workers across the United States. It directs the Department of Transportation to award grants to a qualified nonprofit organization to operate the center and carry out its programs. The TWC provides training, technical assistance, data analysis, and outreach to improve workforce development and transit system performance. Overall, its goal is to strengthen the transit workforce so systems can operate more safely, efficiently, and reliably.

One Fair Price Act: This legislation would prevent companies from setting individualized prices based on consumers' personal data and allow small businesses to better compete with large companies on the quality of their product, not the use of exploitative pricing practices.

Food Date Labeling Act: This bipartisan legislation provides a clear, common-sense solution by establishing a national labeling standard for voluntary use by food manufacturers. Food manufacturers opting to include date labels on their products would have the option to select between one of two universally understood date label phrases:
• "BEST If Used By" communicates to consumers that the quality of the food product may begin to deteriorate after the date.
• "USE By" communicates the end of the estimated period of shelf life, after which the product should not be consumed.

No Time to Waste Act: This bill would direct the Department of Agriculture (USDA) to reduce U.S. food loss and waste (FLW) through federal coordination, grants, and education.

A resolution designating March 21, 2026, as "National Women in Agriculture Day". **(Passed the Senate!)**

A resolution honoring the life and legacy of Reverend Jesse Louis Jackson, Sr., and commending him for his significant leadership during the Civil Rights Movement and his decades of advocacy in pursuit of justice, equality, and human rights. **(Passed the Senate!) **

**In the Community **
I toured the Kent County EMS headquarters and met the dedicated professionals who serve our community around the clock. With new federal funding for a backup generator, their lifesaving work can continue without disruption, no matter what. Our first responders deserve nothing less.

Society is judged by its treatment of children. I spoke at the National Network for Youth Congressional Briefing about my Bipartisan Homeless Children and Youth Act with Senator Katie Britt. Every young person deserves a safe place to lay their head at night. We will keep fighting.
I was thrilled to host a women's business roundtable alongside the Maryland Women's Business Center and the Frederick County Office of Economic Development to engage with women business leaders and owners in celebration of Women's History Month.

Celebrating Women's History Month with H3R! Investing in women and girls is how we build the future. From financial literacy to digital access and emerging markets, when women rise, our entire economy grows. Proud to support the next generation of leaders and wealth builders.

It was my honor to participate in the 37th Annual Delta Days in the Nation's Capital with my sisters of Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Inc. One Delta. One Mission. One Strategy. United in the fight to protect our democracy and deliver for our communities.
I was also thrilled to gather with Delta members of Congress as well as Deltas from across Maryland during a breakfast to strategize as our nation faces real challenges. As Deltas, we know defending our democracy takes courage, and we must push back against efforts like the SAVE Act.

It was a joy to host the first annual Maryland Day celebration in the Senate! I'm proud to stand with Senator Chris Van Hollen and the people who make our state the best in the nation. We stand united by our shared commitment to freedom, opportunity, and a brighter future for all.

**Grant Spotlight **
I'm excited to share some federal grant opportunities for Marylanders. While it's rare that the federal government offers grants that individuals can apply for, I am happy to provide you two opportunities that have recently been announced.

[National Endowment for the Humanities Fellowships](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15517.17616517.6049417.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.grants.gov%2fsearch-results-detail%2f361385&redir_log=425469080857340)
NEH Fellowships are grants to individual scholars pursuing projects that embody exceptional humanistic research, rigorous analysis, and clear writing. Applications must clearly articulate a project's value to humanities scholars, general audiences, or both. These awards provide recipients with time to write, to travel, and to conduct research and other project-related activities. NEH encourages submissions from independent scholars and junior scholars. Projects are eligible at any stage. The 2026 Fellowships competition will accept only projects for research in American history and culture and Western civilization.

[Agriculture and Food Research Initiative Competitive Grants Program Education and Workforce Development](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15517.17616517.6049417.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.grants.gov%2fsearch-results-detail%2f361169&redir_log=434281468423340)
The Agriculture and Food Research Initiative - Education and Workforce Development (EWD) focuses on developing the next generation of research, education, and extension professionals in the food and agricultural sciences. The National Institute of Food and Agriculture (NIFA) requests applications for the AFRI's Education and Workforce Development program areas to support:
1\. professional development opportunities for K-14 educational professionals;
2\. non-formal education that cultivates food and agricultural interest in youth;
3\. workforce training at community, junior, and technical colleges;
4\. training of undergraduate students in research and extension;
5\. fellowships for predoctoral candidates;
6\. fellowships for postdoctoral scholars; and
7\. education and workforce development workshop grants.

**Below is a grant for nonprofits, public housing/Indian housing authorities, and resident associations. **
[Community Development Disaster Prevention and Relief Environment Health](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15517.17616517.6049417.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.grants.gov%2fsearch-results-detail%2f361206&redir_log=840403717565339)
This is a grant through the Department of Housing and Urban Development. ROSS Rapid Response Program (RRP) awards one-time assistance via a cost-reimbursable grant for service coordination and limited direct services for residents of HUD-assisted housing. The RRP utilizes a simplified application process to promote local leadership and flexibility in addressing urgent social needs caused by unanticipated emergencies. Examples of these emergencies can include but are not limited to: • Natural disasters (e.g., wildfires or hurricanes) • Public health crises (e.g., gun violence, community-level contamination or environmental hazards) • Economic disruptions (e.g., closure of a major employment center that employs residents at the target site). **Stay in the Fight ** I know these are difficult times. But please know that I will continue fighting for you every step of the way. We will not give up. We will not give in to this Administration, and I ask that you continue to fight alongside us. Please continue to reach out to us. You can call the office or connect with us at [alsobrooks.senate.gov](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15517.17616517.6049417.7190525&report_id=&redirect=http%3a%2f%2falsobrooks.senate.gov%2f&redir_log=346519414955204). You can also follow us on Bluesky, Instagram, Facebook, Threads, YouTube, and X. We are in this TOGETHER. Sincerely, Angela D. Alsobrooks
United States Senator

We will not give in to this Administration, and I ask that you continue to fight alongside us. Please continue to reach out to us. You can call the office or connect with us at . You can also follow us on Bluesky, Instagram, Facebook, Threads, YouTube, and X. We are in this TOGETHER. Sincerely, Angela D. Alsobrooks United States Senator

name: The Grant Institute
subject: Grant Report: April 2, 2026
body:
The Impact of a Nationwide Ballot Return Deadline By Justin Riemer, President, USGI - Last week, the Supreme Court heard oral argument in Watson...

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/grantdemocracy/grant-report-february-5-12772280?e=c16f400a56)
---
[|
---](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=63476b7478&e=c16f400a56)
| | **The Impact of a Nationwide Ballot Return Deadline**
**By Justin Riemer, President, USGI** Last week, the Supreme Court heard oral argument in _Watson v. Republican National Committee_ , a case that will determine whether federal law requires the return of mail ballots by Election Day. We covered the legal arguments in _Watson_ in an earlier [Grant Report](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=8c4c371dde&e=c16f400a56), and now want to briefly unpack the policy ramifications if the Supreme Court rules in the RNC’s favor.Only [fourteen states](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=4d518a2925&e=c16f400a56) permit a default post-Election Day ballot return, although several among those are universal or heavily vote-by-mail including Oregon, Washington, Nevada, and California. Others are high-population states—including Texas, Illinois, and New York—but have significantly lower mail voting rates. In theory, a large number of voters could be impacted.However, in these states only a small percentage of voters overall take advantage of grace periods. A Votebeat [survey](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=20265ca347&e=c16f400a56) found that late arriving mail ballots represented anywhere between .01 to 3.1% of the 2024 General Election total turnout in states that provided data. Overall, the number of ballots received after Election Day in the 2024 General Election appears to be between 725,000 and 750,000. It’s unclear whether that includes military and overseas (“UOCAVA”) or late arriving ballots that wouldn’t have met even the extended deadline.Ultimately, this ruling should impact only a tiny fraction of the overall electorate, and only a small percentage of mail voters. And impact would undoubtedly be mitigated by voters simply adapting to the deadline by mailing their ballot back earlier, returning it in-person, or simply voting in-person. Making sure voters know of the change certainly puts the onus on state and local election officials, who may need to act quickly to educate voters assuming the ruling affects this year’s General Election. But if voters in heavy or all vote-by-mail states like Arizona or Colorado can successfully navigate an Election Day deadline, there is every reason to believe those in Washington or Oregon can too.Some have raised concerns about the potential impact on UOCAVA voters, but there is good reason to think they are overstated. In addition to existing federal protections, there appears to be a consensus that state carve-outs specifically allowing UOCAVA voters to return ballots after Election Day would survive a ruling in RNC’s favor. However, states with a more blanket post-election day deadline may need to enact UOCAVA specific legislation.An RNC win would also head off a lot of potential controversy and litigation regarding whether ballots were mailed by Election Day. States use a postmark date to determine whether a ballot was timely returned, and postmarks are becoming increasingly unreliable given Postal Service mail processing changes. Although USPS [insists](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=3dfba82a4b&e=c16f400a56) it has not modified postmarking, “adjustments . . . to . . . transportation operations . . . will result in some mailpieces not arriving at . . . originating processing facilities on the same day they are mailed.” Since mail is postmarked at processing facilities, these changes will almost certainly result in unreliable postmarking that officials use to determine whether a ballot met the mailing deadline. As USPS consolidates processing facilities, this problem is only going to grow. Finally, state laws allowing the counting of ballots returned with illegible or even missing postmarks also instigate disputes, something that could now become moot.And for all the hoopla, other issues impact mail voters far more than return deadlines. Data from the Election Assistance Commission’s [EAVS report](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=808e95aac2&e=c16f400a56) indicate that only 17.8% of rejected mail ballots were rejected for not meeting deadlines, the third most common disqualifier. States can do far more to reduce the number of rejected ballots by improving cure processes and adopting more objective (and effective) verification procedures than signature matching.Finally, although some may bemoan that the courts may determine such a significant election policy, it would be one that is broadly popular. A recent poll by [Honest Elections Project](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=198d5354e8&e=c16f400a56) found that 83% of Americans support an election day deadline, and a broad majority agrees that post-election delivery deadlines endanger the public’s trust in elections. Although proponents of ballot return grace periods may think such skepticism is misplaced, no amount of education will change overall sentiment on a policy that most Americans feel is just intuitively wrong. Given the proven link between decreased voter confidence and participation it’s quite possible that improved public confidence in American elections will more than offset any negative impacts from the Supreme Court’s ruling.
---
| | | | |
---
| | **Arizona** The Maricopa County Attorney’s Office [received the names of 207 possible non-citizen](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=cf1d38badf&e=c16f400a56) registered voters to investigate their eligibility. Out of the 207, 60 have previously voted.**California** Sheriff Chad Bianco [commenced an audit of 650,000 ballots](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=4b6bb510ad&e=c16f400a56) from the 2025 election, where voters narrowly decided to authorize the redrawing of California’s congressional districts maps. Bianco initiated his investigation after a local citizens group claimed that the election was falsely inflated by more than 45,000 votes. State Attorney General Rob Bonta and the UCLA Voting Rights Project filed lawsuits challenging his legal authority to gather the materials and Bianco soon after [announced](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=e7f4137dff&e=c16f400a56) he was pausing his probe.**Maryland** The State Administrator of Elections is testing [new digital voting machines](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=d5dc23afb9&e=c16f400a56) slated to be introduced in 2018. Hand-marked paper ballots will still be available to voters.**Michigan** A [second defendant has been sentenced](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=31431db25a&e=c16f400a56) in connection with a 2022 Michigan election fraud scheme involving forged petition signatures for several gubernatorial campaigns.**Mississippi** Legislators have passed a [bill](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=0073cda9bd&e=c16f400a56) that will require [County Registrars to utilize a federal system to determine whether an individual is a citizen](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=e949648228&e=c16f400a56) when they register to vote. If an individual is not confirmed as a citizen under their initial research, the individual will be required to provide documentary proof of citizenship upon voting.**Nevada** In a poll conducted by RightCount Nevada, [80% of respondents answered that the federal government should not have control over elections.](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=a33c8ee531&e=c16f400a56) The poll also found that 51% of respondents expressed support for requiring mail in ballots to be received by the closing of polls.**North Carolina** Senate Republican Leader Phil Berger has [conceded his primary election](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=7bf9c3342c&e=c16f400a56) race after a second recount placed him 23 votes behind his opponent.**Oregon** Secretary of State Read has weighed in on _Watson v. RNC_ , arguing in favor of a [grace period for mail ballots cast and received after election day.](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=861b72e8e8&e=c16f400a56) Oregon conducts all-mail elections and has allowed a seven-day grace period to receive ballots since 2022.**Pennsylvania** The Berks County Commissioners [have delayed voting](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=362a4dd737&e=c16f400a56) on whether to purchase high-speed scanners to tabulate mail ballots until after Congress determines the fate of the SAVE Act.Chester County Election Director Karen Barsoum has announced that [she will leave her post](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=8e9c761d2e&e=c16f400a56) after the state’s primary election this June. This announcement comes after the poll book error in the 2025 election and misprinted names on mail-in ballot applications.**Utah** Utah’s [redistricting](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=3ae6355845&e=c16f400a56) law will not be on the ballot in the upcoming election after a successful removal campaign resulted in organizers failing to secure the required number of petition signatures.**Virginia** Governor Spanberger has signed an [executive order](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=b3a3fb27b9&e=c16f400a56) requiring that [the state rejoin the Electronic Registration Information Center compact](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=bb71913245&e=c16f400a56). Republican National Committee , a case that will determine whether federal law requires the return of mail ballots by Election Day. We covered the legal arguments in Watson in an earlier , and now want to briefly unpack the policy ramifications if the Supreme Court rules in the RNC’s favor.Only permit a default post-Election Day ballot return, although several among those are universal or heavily vote-by-mail including Oregon, Washington, Nevada, and California. Others are high-population states—including Texas, Illinois, and New York—but have significantly lower mail voting rates. In theory, a large number of voters could be impacted.However, in these states only a small percentage of voters overall take advantage of grace periods. A Votebeat found that late arriving mail ballots represented anywhere between .01 to 3.1% of the 2024 General Election total turnout in states that provided data. Overall, the number of ballots received after Election Day in the 2024 General Election appears to be between 725,000 and 750,000. It’s unclear whether that includes military and overseas (“UOCAVA”) or late arriving ballots that wouldn’t have met even the extended deadline.Ultimately, this ruling should impact only a tiny fraction of the overall electorate, and only a small percentage of mail voters. And impact would undoubtedly be mitigated by voters simply adapting to the deadline by mailing their ballot back earlier, returning it in-person, or simply voting in-person. Making sure voters know of the change certainly puts the onus on state and local election officials, who may need to act quickly to educate voters assuming the ruling affects this year’s General Election. But if voters in heavy or all vote-by-mail states like Arizona or Colorado can successfully navigate an Election Day deadline, there is every reason to believe those in Washington or Oregon can too.Some have raised concerns about the potential impact on UOCAVA voters, but there is good reason to think they are overstated. In addition to existing federal protections, there appears to be a consensus that state carve-outs specifically allowing UOCAVA voters to return ballots after Election Day would survive a ruling in RNC’s favor. However, states with a more blanket post-election day deadline may need to enact UOCAVA specific legislation.An RNC win would also head off a lot of potential controversy and litigation regarding whether ballots were mailed by Election Day. States use a postmark date to determine whether a ballot was timely returned, and postmarks are becoming increasingly unreliable given Postal Service mail processing changes. Although USPS it has not modified postmarking, “adjustments . . . to . . . transportation operations . . . will result in some mailpieces not arriving at . . . originating processing facilities on the same day they are mailed.” Since mail is postmarked at processing facilities, these changes will almost certainly result in unreliable postmarking that officials use to determine whether a ballot met the mailing deadline. As USPS consolidates processing facilities, this problem is only going to grow. Finally, state laws allowing the counting of ballots returned with illegible or even missing postmarks also instigate disputes, something that could now become moot.And for all the hoopla, other issues impact mail voters far more than return deadlines. Data from the Election Assistance Commission’s indicate that only 17.8% of rejected mail ballots were rejected for not meeting deadlines, the third most common disqualifier. States can do far more to reduce the number of rejected ballots by improving cure processes and adopting more objective (and effective) verification procedures than signature matching.Finally, although some may bemoan that the courts may determine such a significant election policy, it would be one that is broadly popular. A recent poll by found that 83% of Americans support an election day deadline, and a broad majority agrees that post-election delivery deadlines endanger the public’s trust in elections. Although proponents of ballot return grace periods may think such skepticism is misplaced, no amount of education will change overall sentiment on a policy that most Americans feel is just intuitively wrong.
