clean_body: | | | This moment is demanding more from all of us, Peter. Across the country, Working Families Party candidates, volunteers, and members are stepping up — taking on the establishment, winning tough fights, and building power for working people at every level. Here’s just some of what the Working Families Party has been up to over the past month: BUILDING POWER IN 2026... FROM THE GROUND UP: While we’re going full speed to take back the House and Senate from Republicans in 2026 and elect working families champions to replace them, we’re also focused on building power where it starts: in our states and local communities. Over the past month, WFP and our chapters across the country have started knocking on doors, talking to voters, and organizing our neighbors to elect working families champions running at every level of government — from school boards and county commissions to state legislatures and mayors. (And this is just a snapshot, Peter.) In Georgia , that includes Ruwa Romman for State Senate, District 7, along with Aaron Baker , Kenn Collier , Jyot Singh , Michelle Kang , Alana Sanders , Gabriel Sanchez , Bryce Berry , and Marvin Lim for State House. We’re also supporting Keyanna Jones Moore for DeKalb County Commission and Kerry Hatcher and Adrienne Simmons for local school boards. In New Jersey , we’ve endorsed Ron Bautista and David Gurgis in Hudson County and Ali Aljarrah in Passaic for County Commissioners. In Pennsylvania , we’re backing Sara Agerton , Ce-Ce Gerlach , Sierra McNeil , and Chris Johnson for State House. In Oregon , we’ve endorsed Isabella Lee Tibbetts for Jackson County Commission, Myrna Muñoz for State Senate, District 15, and John (Waz) Wasielewski for State House, District 38. And in Ohio , we’re supporting Bryan Hambley for Secretary of State, Davida Russell for State Representative in HD-18, and Charity Martin King for State Representative in HD-2, alongside the Columbus “Our City, Our Voice” ballot measure. These are just some of the candidates we’ve endorsed in the past month, Peter. Across every region of the country, we’re backing many more working families champions — both incumbents and challengers — who are rooted in their communities and ready to take on corporate power and right-wing attacks, and to fight for housing, healthcare, good jobs, and dignity for all. HOLDING U.S. SENATOR JOHN FETTERMAN ACCOUNTABLE: We’re also laying the groundwork to hold elected officials accountable when they turn their backs on working people. In Pennsylvania, that means John Fetterman. Over the past year, Fetterman has repeatedly sided with the far right — including voting with Republicans to block a War Powers Resolution to stop Trump’s war on Iran , and reversing his position on voter ID laws , going from calling them “insidious” to backing them despite the barriers they create for working-class voters and communities of color. Last month, Pennsylvania WFP made it clear: we’re building toward a future primary challenge — recruiting a strong candidate, organizing statewide, and holding Fetterman accountable every step of the way. We’ve launched as a hub for this work, and we’re building the long-term campaign it will take to recruit a strong challenger, organize statewide, and replace him with leadership that is accountable to working people — not corporate power or political convenience. Because this is bigger than one senator. Across the country, too many politicians campaign with working people, then govern for the wealthy. We’re not waiting until the last minute to challenge that — we’re building power now. JUSTICE FOR US: The Working Families Party’sCriminal Justice Initiative recently notched notable wins in its work to build power to disrupt mass incarceration and systems that disproportionately affect working people. In Arkansas, Bobby Forrest Jr. defeated an incumbent backed by Governor Sarah Huckabee Sanders to become Prosecuting Attorney for the 6th Judicial District, covering Pulaski and Perry Counties — a major victory for accountability and reform. In North Carolina, CJI supported incumbent District Attorney Satana Deberry in her re-election in Durham County, where she’s building an office that prioritizes diversion and restorative justice. In Mecklenburg County, Sheriff Garry McFadden also secured another term after ending the county’s 287(g) program that led to the deportation of 15,000 county residents. These wins reflect a growing momentum to dismantle systems of mass incarceration and build a justice system rooted in care, accountability, and real safety for our communities. SAY LESS, OREGON WFP: Oregon Working Families Party’s growing influence is getting noticed. A recent pointed out the Party’s lack of an endorsement in the upcoming gubernatorial primary — a sign of its political weight. Instead, Oregon WFP endorsed a of municipal and state legislative candidates who center the struggles of working people. That strategy is delivering results. Oregon’s legislative session just wrapped with major wins, including an immigrant rights package with $111 million to protect SNAP participants, $2 million in emergency support for refugees and immigrants, and $8 million to expand legal services for children and families separated from a caregiver. Oregon WFP also helped lead the push to keep hundreds of millions of dollars in the state by partially disconnecting from the federal tax code. While not the full measure advocates pushed for, it helps fill a budget gap and prevent cuts to essential services. The bill is expected to be signed by Gov. Tina Kotek. Shoutout to WFP champions Rep. Farrah Chaichi , Rep. Lesly Muñoz , Rep. Willy Chotzen , Sen. Kayse Jama , and Sen. Winsvey Campos for getting the people’s business done in Salem. BUILDING WFP IN NORTH CAROLINA: In North Carolina, Working Families Party candidates have been taking on the establishment — and winning. In HD-106, Rodney Sadler unseated a Democratic incumbent who sided with Republicans and supported cooperation with ICE — a decisive break from politics that criminalize and abandon working people. WFP champions Renée Ann Price and Rodney Pierce also won re-election, continuing to build power for communities too often shut out of decision-making. And although Nida Allam fell just one point short in the Durham-area congressional primary, her campaign made clear how close we are to breaking through — even while being outspent two-to-one by AI and AIPAC money. These races show both the scale of what we’re up against and how close we are to breaking through — with working people organizing to challenge the status quo and win bigger fights ahead. NEW MEXICO STATE LEGISLATORS TO GET PAID: In a major step toward a more representative democracy, New Mexico lawmakers passed a long -overdue proposal to pay state legislators — breaking down a key barrier that has kept working people out of office. New Mexico is the last state in the country with an unpaid legislature, forcing everyday people to shoulder the financial burden of serving while wealthy insiders hold onto power. If voters approve the measure this November, legislators would earn about $67,000 a year — roughly the state’s median household income — making it possible for working-class candidates to run and serve without sacrificing their livelihoods. The proposal, backed by New Mexico WFP, is already facing opposition from oil and gas interests and wealthy lawmakers who benefit from the status quo. Now, New Mexico WFP is helping lead the fight to win at the ballot — educating voters on what’s at stake and building support to open the doors of government to working people. NO MORE ENDLESS WAR: Across the country, working people are speaking out against another devastating war — and making it clear: we refuse to let more violence be carried out in our name. Earlier this month, we asked our supporters to weigh in through a on the war in Iran. The responses were clear: people are scared, angry, and overwhelmingly opposed to this war. What’s unfolding is devastating. Families are being torn apart, communities are living in fear, and people are being forced to endure violence they did not choose. And war isn’t just fought overseas. It puts American troops’ lives on the line, drives up costs for working people here at home, and pulls billions of dollars away from healthcare, housing, education, and the things our communities actually need. This is a political choice. Time and again, we’re told there’s no money for working people — but there is always money for war. Meanwhile, politicians in Washington continue to escalate violence while ignoring the real needs of the people they represent. BIG TECH IS DRIVING UP COSTS. WE’RE ORGANIZING TO FIGHT BACK: Across the country, working people are seeing their utility bills rise — even when their usage hasn’t changed. One major driver: AI data centers. These facilities are driving up electricity demand, draining water, increasing pollution, and reshaping communities — while utility companies pass the costs onto us and guarantee profits for Big Tech. We’re organizing to push back, and we’re looking for people ready to step up. VIDEO OF THE WEEK: Taylor Rehmet , endorsed by Texas Working Families Party, just won a special election for State Senate in a Trump +17 district — a major upset that shows what’s possible when working people organize. UPCOMING EVENTS: Looking for a way to get involved with WFP and have an hour to spare? Join our weekly WFP Call Party Power Hour to make calls with your fellow WFP volunteers from anywhere! Whether you’re a long-time WFP member or just getting started, we’re inviting you to join our April Welcome Gathering! At the Welcome Gathering, WFP members and activists will get concrete about how we’re building the power we need to have an impact in this political moment, and help you figure out the best ways to get involved. Join our next Mass Call on Monday, April 27 at 8PM ET, where members of our movement will unpack what’s happening in this moment and how we organize to build a government for the many, not the few. Thank you for taking the time to read this month’s update, Peter — and for being part of this movement. The fights ahead are big. Taking back Congress, challenging corporate power, and building real governing power for working people will take all of us. Everything you read here — from electing candidates to organizing in communities across the country — is powered by people like you. In solidarity, Team WFP Thoughts? Feedback? We want to hear it. Reply directly to this email and let us know. This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. If you received this email as a forward and want to get the latest updates from the Working Families Party directly, The Working Families Party is the party of the multiracial working class, fighting for a nation that cares for all of us. Wanna learn more? And if you need to update your contact information, Other political groups have corporate donors. But we can pool our resources too. _“Faster than Chick-fil-a.”_
That’s how UT Austin students Rama and Reela described getting registered to vote when Beto spoke with them on campus:

Across Texas, there are young people like Rama and Reela who are ready to show up in these November elections — if we meet them where they are, make it easy to get registered, and stay connected all the way through Election Day.
Beto is already looking to get back out on the road soon: visiting more campuses, meeting more students, and helping even more young Texans get registered and ready to vote.
That’s the work we’re doing at Powered by People.
We’re organizing across this state to reach, register, and turn out the voters who will decide the future of Texas. But our ability to do that depends on the resources we have to support our organizers and volunteers.

I wanted to send you a quick note to say thank you.
# [](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1269?t=1&akid=3052%2E21716%2Ek5Pne9)
Hi, it's Sarah.
I wanted to send you a quick note to say _thank you._ Because of the incredible support of this grassroots community we reached our end-of-quarter fundraising goal ahead of last night’s deadline.

Hi Derek, — it’s Lorenza Ramirez, the DNC’s National Organizing Director. I wanted to reach out with a big update on our work to win the midterms this year.
**I am thrilled to announce that this week we unveiled our[ 2026 DNC Playbook](https://democrats.org/playbook/?refcode=em_20260402_6594_fr&akid=6594%2E22930333%2EFw845P).** This is a comprehensive guide for state parties and campaigns filled with the guidance, resources, and best practices they need to run winning organizing programs this year and into the future.
I’ll be honest with you: The political landscape has shifted in major ways, and traditional methods of running campaigns are falling more and more behind. Democrats _need_ to continue evolving our approach to organizing if we want a shot at flipping the House and the Senate and winning down-ballot races across the country this year.
**Here are the three most important things you need to know:**
1️⃣ The Playbook is a resource rooted in actionable strategies that we’ve seen have real success. We’ve included case studies, research, and community insights so campaigns can study winning strategies and adapt them to their own communities, districts, and states.
2️⃣ We’ve introduced three critical shifts every organizing program should embrace in order to win, starting with changing how we talk to voters. This includes a new conversation model, metrics, and best practices to have high-quality, listening-first conversations with voters. These shifts are focused on expanding our organizing tactics and prioritizing real conversations with voters over a number on a page.
**3️⃣ We’re not just looking at the next election — we’re looking at building up long-term Democratic infrastructure that will help us win far into the future.**

The DNC is the _only_ organization working to elect Democrats at all levels of government, all over the country, _every single year_.

**But a judge may have just SAVED the future of public media, declaring Trump’s attacks a direct violation of the First Amendment!**

[**This is proof that our fight is WORKING. So we’re gathering 15,000 signatures to celebrate this incredible victory and THANK public broadcasters for refusing to back down »**](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/106281?t=7&akid=23460%2E878179%2Ef7AZ6E) | [**Stand with Public Broadcasters: Chip in $3 to sign now »**](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/106281?t=8&akid=23460%2E878179%2Ef7AZ6E)
---
TO: Public Broadcasters
FROM: A grateful Democrat
Subject: Thank you! To all public broadcasters,

Thank you. Thank you for enriching all of our lives — in rural and urban areas, and everywhere in between — with your various news and educational programs.

I couldn’t be more THRILLED to see Trump’s disgusting executive order blocked. _His authoritarian power grab didn’t stand a chance against our fight._

**I also know that Trump’s attacks on the free press don’t end here — he wants to shut down MS NOW, CNN, and anyone else who holds him accountable.**

It’s not just upsetting, _it’s a dangerous step towards an**outright dictatorship!**_ That’s why I’m not getting complacent.

[**I’m signing this letter today by chipping in $3 to VPP to thank you for your years of service and to join VPP in the fight against Trump’s attacks on the free press. | | Peter,
---
| | Charlie Kirk lived fast. And he lived loud.

He filled arenas. He lit a fire in the next generation on campus.

He confronted lies and spoke truth with boldness.

And he built a movement and a machine that few ever thought possible.

I saw it up close -- _Charlie moved at a pace most couldn 't keep up with. _

But in the middle of all the noise... he made a quiet decision that changed everything.

_**He started observing the Sabbath. **_

Not as a box to check. Not as a religious performance.

_But as an act of obedience. _

As a way of saying, **_" God, You are enough. And because You are enough, I need not carry the weight of a world that was never mine to hold." _**

Every week -- no matter what -- Charlie stopped.

He turned off the noise. He stepped away from the battlefield.

No email. No media. No work.

He gave his full attention fully to God, his wife Erika, and his children.

It was hard at first -- for someone who carried so much.

But over time, it changed him.

And before he was assassinated, he wrote a book about what he had learned...

name: AOC
subject: Mosaics
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
Just because we didn’t see the big picture at first doesn’t mean we weren’t part of one.
#
Sometimes people will ask me, “There is so much happening in the world and in the country, and it all feels so big and overwhelming - what can I even do as one person?” What I try to convey every time is that no action is too small, and if you feel so moved, you can and should start with whatever is within arm’s reach or in your backyard. You can even start with yourself.
We live in a culture of grand gestures and big ambitions, but that also means we should be wary of how much “get-rich-quick” thinking can perpetuate beyond money schemes and into the idea that any/all major, impactful shifts happen suddenly and in dramatic fashion with a handful of major figures. The fact is, that couldn’t be further from the truth. Revolutionary and transformative changes, from the inside out, happen more like mosaics.
[](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260402.DvvDG6&refcode=em20260402-11106-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=11106%2E2526796%2E7Or9Y0)
Think of it like this: no matter who we are, how visible or invisible or big or small, each one of us is just one tile. Whether you see that as liberating or disempowering is a matter of perspective. When you have your eye pressed all the way up to the single tile of a mosaic, it can look quite meaningless. A single piece of shattered glass could look worthless. Or perhaps a piece of small painted porcelain could seem beautiful, but too small to “be” anything. Or maybe a stunning rare slab of stone may think itself as the biggest piece when it is really a corner tile. The secret is, it’s all significant.
**The two secrets of mosaics are:**
1. Each piece (us + our small actions) is far more powerful and meaningful than we know, and
2. Each piece (we) need each other far more than we realize.

When we are able to step back from thinking our own broken, unfinished pieces are not enough, and start to see how all the other little pieces glistening alongside us start to form eyes and ears and abstract beauty and landscapes and symbols and more, we realize that just because we didn’t see the big picture at first doesn’t mean we weren’t part of one.
So just do the small thing - for yourself and others. Choose your actions with humility, love, and enthusiasm. **It means more than you know, and the world thanks you for it**.
Take heart,
Alexandria

| | On Tuesday, Trump issued his latest executive order designed to limit access to mail-in voting for this year's midterm elections. Trump's unconstitutional order is voter suppression, plain and simple. It would direct the DHS and Social Security Administration to make a list of eligible voters in each state, and have a say over who is able to vote by mail. Let's call this out for what it is: **a last-ditch effort by a president with cratering approval ratings to rig the vote before the American people deliver a verdict on his cuts to health care, his war of choice with Iran, his tariffs that have driven the cost of living higher, and his covering up of the Epstein files.** Oregon has been voting by mail for over thirty years. It's safe, easy, and effective. Mail-in voting has fewer instances of fraud than any other method of voting, and for many seniors, disabled folks, and rural Americans, it is the only way they're able to make their voices heard in our Democratic process. | | | **[He’s getting worse, and he needs to be removed from office](https://default.salsalabs.org/T7ee947db-b950-47e5-a244-9dd5200228a2/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9).** We’ve seen evidence before, of course, but this wasn’t just “Trump being Trump,” this took it to a whole new level. The nation is scared, the world is scared, and he must be removed by any legal means ASAP. Yes, it’s going to be hard. body:
The cost of AI is growing
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260402-2681)
Peter,
Yesterday, We Energies — Wisconsin's largest utility, serving more than a million households — filed with state regulators for a [14.75% residential rate hike](https://act.francescahong.com/go/10329?t=1&akid=2681%2E105371%2EhmfC7y). If approved, it would be the sixth increase since 2020.
Why is this happening? Blame AI. We Energies is spending $6 billion on new power generation, and hyperscale data centers — like Microsoft's campus in Mount Pleasant — are driving most of that new demand.
We Energies says they have a plan to keep data center costs off your bill. But the state's own analysts found [loopholes](https://act.francescahong.com/go/10330?t=2&akid=2681%2E105371%2EhmfC7y) — including a cost-sharing arrangement where residential customers still pick up 25% of the tab for new gas plants built to serve data centers, plus all fuel costs. Wisconsin's Citizens Utility Board called it "another double-digit increase for customers who have already seen their bills rise much faster than inflation."
Also this week: Researchers at the University of Cambridge found that AI data centers are creating ["heat islands"](https://act.francescahong.com/go/10331?t=3&akid=2681%2E105371%2EhmfC7y) — warming surrounding land by up to 16 degrees Fahrenheit and affecting an estimated 340 million people worldwide. That’s a serious hazard. Heat islands mean worse heat waves, worse air quality, and real health risks — especially for the communities closest to these facilities.
There are already more than 3,000 data centers operating in the U.S., with nearly 1,500 more planned or under construction. These facilities are being fast-tracked into communities without adequate protections for the people who live there.
My CONTROL-ALT-DELETE plan calls for a moratorium on data center construction until we know how to protect ourselves from their environmental and energy costs. If a community decides it wants to build a data center, any new construction must use union labor and follow three rules:
* No tax breaks for private profit — Wisconsin already handed out $40 million in data center subsidies last fiscal year
* Fund new renewable or clean energy infrastructure with strict environmental protections
* Infrastructure must be publicly owned — so whatever the long-term outcome of data centers, we build something useful for all Wisconsinites

Our wallets, our environment, and our future is at stake.
**[Please chip in whatever you can - $5, $15, $25 - so this campaign can keep fighting.](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260402.O5Na-q&refcode=em20260402-2681&t=4&akid=2681%2E105371%2EhmfC7y) **
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260402.O5Na-q&amount=5&refcode=em20260402-2681&t=23&akid=2681%2E105371%2EhmfC7y)**
In solidarity,
Fran

body:
After all you’ve done for our Party, I salute you, Patriot!
| Patriot,
---
I’m sick of seeing text messages that accuse you of abandoning the GOP after all you’ve done for us.
---
All because you didn’t give $15 before some random deadline, that’s supposed to mean you **_“betrayed”_** the Republican Party and became a Democrat?
---
So all the times you stood in line to vote, you knocked on doors, you put up a yard sign, you made phone calls, you filled out surveys, you sacrificed your time and money – suddenly, all of that means nothing?
---
**_Give me a break! That’s just insulting._**
---
_Hand to God, I will never stoop to that low._

Truth be told, I try not to write too many emails and texts as it is. I’m busy working in Washington to do the job you asked me to do.

Honestly, fundraising just isn’t Priority #1.

At the end of 2024, I transferred $2.5 MILLION _**away**_ from my own campaign to help conservatives in tough races who _truly_ needed help.

---
| | Patriot,
---
I'm going to be blunt with you.

We are closer to losing this country than most people are willing to admit.

Not someday. Not "if things keep going this way."

Right now.

And the scariest part?

It's not happening in Washington. It's happening in classrooms.

High schools. Colleges.

Places where the next generation is being shaped -- or more accurately... reshaped.

If you've ever looked at what's coming out of our schools and thought: _" What happened to this country?" _

You're not wrong. You're seeing it clearly.

Because while most people are arguing online... while they're hoping things will turn around... while they're waiting for the next election to fix everything...

The other side is doing something far more dangerous.

They're raising the next generation.

Earlier. Faster. And with zero resistance in most places.

That's how countries are lost.

Slowly. Then all at once.

But here's the thing that should give a patriot like you hope...

There is one place where that trend is actually being challenged.

_And it shouldn 't even exist. _

**Just one year ago, Turning Point USA 's high school program -- which is now called "Club America" -- was in about 1,200 schools.**
That alone felt like a miracle.

Because starting even ONE chapter today takes courage most adults don't have.

Conservative students get mocked. Targeted. Threatened. Shut down.

And yet...

_They stepped up anyway. _

About that time, Charlie called me.

He didn't sound optimistic... He sounded urgent.

"Andrew, we've got to move faster."

I told him we were. He stopped me.

"No. You're not thinking what I'm thinking. I want to be in 35,000 high schools."

I actually laughed.

"Charlie... there aren't even 35,000 high schools in America."

"Okay," he said. "How many are there?"

"About 27,000."

And without hesitation: "Good. Let's do 27,000."

I remember sitting there thinking to myself... we're barely in 1,200 schools.

We didn't have the staff. We didn't have the infrastructure. We didn't even have the roadmap yet.

But Charlie wasn't fazed.

_" We'll figure it out." _

That was him.

He didn't wait for perfect conditions.

Because he knew something most people don't want to face: If we wait... _we lose everything. _

And now?

Less than a year later...
---
[](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=3b7744adc48c4847bbeec41a8e9d260e&_e=9gi740LydYPPPagVHT3DV73mV0MbecjqYKxVZUo7qEHfep-vXUPoZtDVkOxrFaZNDjE4lTsb52jWgoisV9XNvdQWTrCR3qyy1Qarg9R_XkIq-JK7vnm9YqqnJdz9m5XdScNchSFWAhzP3Z_OiaJay7DFMZkru1mscHNE6fOU7_DRvXuq3sSusqjLjMuqVaXQ5xiiN0pdIdgAJu-rbjTPxZrdLmt4ALVYkjzj-Dn9JjDuRL4BUL9oduTOnosgs_p34YsW-cCbECJm0ohLLujsZ2mevo1p7OA1pMzBefjLw5QuZ4z56L4eTURxHpFQYSGabsWcOwiWD7Hwp5fZPI1zemqAwXYtX5ncjiRJeX0u90kyAt2BKcTWMA19H2SPk6I49_7vQ0g0WawLcU3g0-A-Pr9tykoSGqVDPcH1RTjimrhbW5Sm1CF70AWwuwq_yhQR5n0troBdRzWg8B3uU9leWHG6rMly4NL4Gc7UXoBjiOrnKeLBWWYItooi3plSeK0PNSesro7BBmwLQixWTRBn8FEIcenQC-_D0ClqlCxn9CDrC_ZHUj0HvGTAHJSBmqMexHeph3oP6CbhwnUPwmaVFUnYiD5wO2BBM9b3uyJ_W25-liXhUOKSrl5DjbAQCOMe6kYAJdfxr-V6VwdyOiYBZAPy2eSTHFtA3NmEZYtoO00-nqMj5qgs8ABbPO6gOj6B5L07x1bXrqandoOOXboGog%3D%3D)
---
**We 're in 3,300 schools. **

**Thirteen percent of all high schools in America. **

**Eight states are now backing this effort to put a Club America chapter in every high school statewide. **

_That shouldn 't be possible. _

Not in this environment. Not with the level of hostility these students face every single day.

And yet... it's still happening.

_But Patriot, here 's the part you need to understand: _

This is not a victory. It's a foothold.

_Because in the other 87% of schools? _

There is no resistance. None.

Just one-sided propaganda from the Left.

One-sided pressure on kids who are too young to even realize what's happening to them.

That's the reality.

The question isn't whether we're fighting. We are.

The question is whether it's enough.

Because right now, the students stepping up through Club America...

They're not the majority. _They 're the exception. _

They're the ones willing to take the heat.

The ones willing to stand alone.

The ones willing to risk being targeted just to say: _" I love this country." _
---
[](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=3b7744adc48c4847bbeec41a8e9d260e&_e=9gi740LydYPPPagVHT3DV73mV0MbecjqYKxVZUo7qEHfep-vXUPoZtDVkOxrFaZNDjE4lTsb52jWgoisV9XNvdQWTrCR3qyy1Qarg9R_XkIq-JK7vnm9YqqnJdz9m5XdScNchSFWAhzP3Z_OiaJay7DFMZkru1mscHNE6fOU7_DRvXuq3sSusqjLjMuqVaXQ5xiiN0pdIdgAJu-rbjTPxZrdLmt4ALVYkjzj-Dn9JjDuRL4BUL9oduTOnosgs_p3lKJMdFC9CGDkXi1XenwCyuQl2TqhPsEYAr6YVYts4xrzESdCWNTCb6iZW7pJqxO8zSR9zb8ATM7wHNqDg89k49CpWC7jgmkoV_VajkFSEOp1gbiiHdg311u2RVjW_xrXn8yTsSo06t0LCjGJVLvg4cdU5tgfWIcD60n3w5Q4TIAi8h7Lhh5HCHMTrEAd1nWu7bBx0egcZuYkLss9_aobd8szBFWQ37yfDg2lXRZGwartwG4gb9AdRjGDkd50u8BIhrOcxKBKS2AlqLgQgVvIeW1AQBKHaBjEfnzXyykCRe6j8MGGTeiXJT0nGSRq-Bvpy3ojKWr0jN7Vlm51LCQm5MMw18wFhdH3DjAcZvIuPNi23bje6FaImUbRf9kBQvaeAlHgeS5Qnsi6sxfmXeGeM6PaaKv0bVlv1-gx664WiebUyvq7hbTepmgOXa3Uk0-oq8lq0p6Gu_5Zsg6wRcHDTQ%3D%3D)
---
And every time one of those students raises their hand...

We have a choice.

Back them. _Or leave them on their own. _

**Because when a student starts a chapter, we send them an activism kit -- with American flags. Pocket Constitutions. Leadership tools. **

Everything they need to actually stand their ground.

Not symbolically. For real.

They've already made the decision to lead.

All they're waiting on... is you and me.

**Each activism kit costs $25. That 's it. **

$25 to make sure one student doesn't have to stand alone against the Left in a hostile school.

* **Just days ago, Trump himself voted by mail** in Florida. Now he wants to restrict that same right for millions of Americans.
* Three federal judges already blocked provisions of a similar Trump order trying to change how elections are run — because **presidents don’t have the power to do this.**
* Naturally,**this tracks back to Putin.** Last summer, Trump declared that he’d try to ban mail voting after hearing from Putin that supposedly “it’s impossible to have mail-in voting and have an honest election.”
* But **mail voting fraud is virtually nonexistent** — only 0.000043% of all mail ballots cast according to a Brookings Institution Report. And when Georgia’s Republican Secretary of State audited 8.2 million voters in 2024, he only found a 0.002% rate of possible irregularities.

#
**Donald Trump and his GOP yes-men are saying the quiet part out loud, Peter.**

| | | | | | Dear Peter,Pam Bondi’s removal was the right decision, but it came far too late to prevent the damage already done or restore confidence in America’s justice system.Our leaders can not drive legal decisions based on political convenience or favoritism for the wealthy elite. We must apply the law equally without political calculation so justice works for all, not just the privileged few. The survivors of Jeffrey Epstein’s crimes, and others harmed by Pam Bondi’s mismanaged policies, deserve justice. Their voices should guide our leaders, not be ignored or sidelined for political gain.The leadership we’re building in CA-32 is focused on serving working people with respect, empathy, and integrity. That’s how we earn trust, uphold accountability, and ensure the government works for everyone, not just the powerful.**If you believe in that vision, I hope you’ll stand with me.**[**Join us today in building a movement that fights for working families, and ensures justice for those harmed by leaders who put politics over people.**](https://chrisahuja.us2.list-manage.com/track/click?u=67424df89870d1cac00e55f46&id=3e576a632a&e=53c7d12fc7)
